subject: Post-call: MedlyRx deployment path (BAA / SOC2 evidence) and next steps
messages:
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
To: Jamie Park <jamie.park@medlyrx.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-18T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call: MedlyRx deployment path (BAA / SOC2 evidence) and next steps

Hi Jamie,

Thanks again for taking the time this morning — appreciated the context on your PHI use cases and the compliance barboard for the pilot. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can keep momentum: 

Summary of requirements you shared
- Primary: BAA required for any production handling of PHI.
- Audit: SOC 2 Type II report required for vendor assessment; you also want the control matrix that maps SOC 2 controls to our operational artifacts.
- Data residency: US-only (preference for us-east region).
- Access: Strict RBAC and audit logs; procurement will want an IP allowlist option for private endpoints.

Deployment tradeoffs we discussed
- Hosted API: fastest to go-live; Redwood's hosted environment supports encryption-in-transit and at-rest and can be covered by a BAA, but customer-managed VPC/network isolation is limited compared to Dedicated/Private.
- Dedicated: reserved GPU pool, tenant isolation, stronger network controls (private egress/VPN options), recommended for steady production throughput with predictable SLAs.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): full network control, customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM), and necessary for strict audit/policy constraints — higher onboarding lead time and procurement complexity.

Immediate asks from your side
- Please confirm whether MedlyRx requires customer-managed keys (CMK) for at-rest encryption or if Redwood-managed KMS is acceptable for the pilot.
- Can you share the procurement timeline and the name/email for the procurement lead so we can align contract/BAA turnaround?
- Jamie — can you confirm whether you need SOC 2 Type II only, or also a point-in-time penetration test report?

Proposed next steps (for our side)
1) I attached a short evidence checklist (security_questionnaire_v2.pdf) that maps the typical SOC 2 asks to the artifacts we can provide.
2) I'll loop in our Security Engineer (Ben) and CS lead (Marissa) to prepare the network diagram and propose one recommended deployment path for the pilot (Hosted + Dedicated fallback or Private if CMK/on-prem required).
3) If you agree, let's schedule a 30 min procurement + security sync next week to review the checklist and timeline.

Attachments included: security_questionnaire_v2.pdf, redwood_network_diagram.png (draft).

Thanks — I’ll follow up internally and share a short action plan by EOD.

Best,
Connor O'Brien
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
connor.obrien@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0132

--
Redwood Inference — Developer-first inference platform for production LLMs
From: Jamie Park <jamie.park@medlyrx.com>

Subject: Re: Post-call: MedlyRx deployment path (BAA / SOC2 evidence) and next steps

Connor — thanks for the recap and the checklist. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) BAA: Yes, MedlyRx requires a signed BAA before any production PHI processing. Procurement will lead on contract language, but we need Redwood's standard BAA template to speed review.

2) SOC 2: We require SOC 2 Type II (most recent 12 months). A control mapping (which controls cover logging/segregation/access) would be very helpful. Pen test report is nice-to-have but not mandatory for the pilot.

3) CMK: For the pilot we're flexible — Redwood-managed KMS is acceptable for the initial phase. If we move to production at scale, we may require customer-managed keys or a Private deployment (TBD).

4) Network: Procurement will request an IP allowlist and support for a dedicated VPC endpoint for production traffic.

Procurement timeline: their estimated review window is 3–4 weeks after we provide the BAA and SOC 2 artifacts. Procurement lead is Priya Natarajan (priya.natarajan@medlyrx.com).

Can you have Ben share a short one-page summary (audit artifact list + expected turnaround) and a recommended pilot deployment? Also please include any pricing delta between Hosted->Dedicated->Private for a 6-month pilot so Procurement can model costs.

Thanks — Jamie
Jamie Park
Head of Clinical Integrations, MedlyRx
jamie.park@medlyrx.com | +1 212-555-0199

Hi team — thanks, quick artifact summary below and a recommended pilot path. See attached DocSend link for SOC 2 and control mapping (https://docsend.com/view/abc123).

Artifact summary (what Redwood can provide immediately)
- SOC 2 Type II report: most recent 12-month period (DocSend link above).
- Control mapping: one-page mapping to common customer questions (included in DocSend bundle).
- Audit logs: streaming audit logs and 90-day export available; longer retention options via a retention add-on.
- BAA: attached (BAA_template.docx) — we can provide a signed BAA on standard terms; highlight if you need tighter data residency clauses.
- Network: draft network diagram attached (redwood_network_diagram.png) showing Hosted (public endpoint + TLS) vs Dedicated (VPC peering / private egress) vs Private (customer VPC / on-prem).

Recommended pilot deployment (given MedlyRx flexibility on KMS):
- Pilot: Hosted API with Dedicated capacity reserved as a fallback. Rationale: fastest onboarding (Hosted) + predictable performance when traffic spikes (Dedicated). This lets you start within 1–2 weeks while procurement reviews BAA and SOC artifacts.
- If MedlyRx later requires CMK or strict network isolation, transition path to Private (VPC) is supported but typically 4–8 weeks for full onboarding and key exchange.

6-month pilot pricing delta (ballpark)
- Hosted-only: baseline usage pricing + per-token.
- Hosted + Dedicated (reserve small GPU pool): ~1.7–2.2x baseline depending on capacity commitment.
- Private VPC/on-prem: higher onboarding fee + infra pass-through costs, typically 2.5–3.5x baseline for initial 6 months.

Next steps
1) Connor: share the DocSend link, attachments, and proposed 30-min sync windows for week of 4/26.
2) Jamie/Priya: confirm procurement availability and go/no-go triggers.

Ben Carter
Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com
